# Documentation Standards

Reference file for documentation conventions across the project.
Read this file when creating or editing documentation, README files, or code comments.

## General Rules

- All documentation files used for code documentation must be in markdown format unless stated otherwise
- File naming: kebab-case for config/reference files (e.g. `git-conventions.md`),
  hyphenated Title-Case for docs (e.g. `Editor-Parity.md`, `docs/Knowledge-Base.md`) *(Kanōn)*
- No icons or emojis in any documentation or code unless explicitly stated otherwise *(Kanōn)*

## File Naming

- Use Title Case for document titles inside the file
- Config/reference files: kebab-case (e.g. `git-conventions.md`)
- Docs: hyphenated Title-Case (e.g. `Editor-Parity.md`, `docs/Knowledge-Base.md`)
- Exception: `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` keep standard names
- Exception: ADR files follow MADR - `ADR-NNN-<kebab-slug>.md` (uppercase prefix)

## Documentation Types

| Type | Location | Purpose | Authored by |
|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `README.md` | project root | Setup, usage, contribution | Human |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | project root | Release history (post-MVP only) | Human + AI |
| `docs/adr/ADR-NNN-*.md` | docs/adr/ | Architecture decision records | AI (auto-captured) |
| `docs/adr/index.md` | docs/adr/ | ADR registry table | AI (auto-maintained) |
| `docs/Knowledge-Base.md` | docs/ | Auto-generated index of all docs | AI (generated) |
| `.kanon/references/*.md` | .kanon/references/ | Convention reference files | Human |

## Architecture and Setup Documents

Applies to architecture, design and setup or deployment docs. Research and deep-dive docs are exempt.

- Focused and to the point; no wall of text. *(Kanōn)*
- Long descriptions become points of at most 3-4 lines, led by a one-line summary.
- Include diagrams (Mermaid or SVG) wherever they clarify a flow, boundary or deployment.
- Rendered output (HTML, PDF, slides) uses Open Sans by default at standard or small sizes; no large type.
- Self-check before writing, and before asking the user: would an engineering manager, a lead
  developer and a principal engineer each grasp it quickly, with full technical rigour and no
  filler? If not, cut prose and add points or a diagram. Ask only when still in doubt.

## Architecture Decision Records

- Stored in `docs/adr/ADR-NNN-<kebab-slug>.md` (zero-padded 3-digit number)
- Use MADR format: Status, Date, Context, Options Considered, Decision, Consequences
- Status values: `Proposed` | `Accepted` | `Deprecated` | `Superseded by ADR-NNN`
- Never edit an accepted ADR's Decision section. Create a new ADR with `Supersedes: ADR-NNN`
- Always committed with the code they relate to, never as a standalone commit *(Kanōn)*
- Source always noted in frontmatter: `brainstorm` | `spec:<filename>` | `plan:<filename>` | `session`
- `docs/adr/index.md` is auto-maintained as a registry table. Do not edit manually *(Kanōn)*

## Knowledge Base

- Acts as a structured index with extracted data, not a narrative summary
- Sections: Project Identity, ADR Registry, Domain Knowledge, Implementation History, Current State, Open Decisions, Tech Debt, Docs Index

## Auto-generated Files

The following files are generated by AI skills. Do not edit directly:

| File | Generated by | Trigger |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `docs/adr/index.md` | `adr-manager` skill | Every ADR write |

## Code Comments

Few comments, each earning its line. A wall of comment text is a defect, the same as dead code. *(Kanōn)*

- **Explain WHY, not WHAT.** The code says what it does; a comment exists only where the
  reason is not recoverable from reading it - a non-obvious constraint, a workaround and the
  bug it works around, an ordering that looks arbitrary but is not.
- **One or two lines.** If the explanation needs a paragraph, it belongs in an ADR or a
  runbook, and the comment links to it.
- **No narration.** No banner headers, no `// increment counter`, no restating the signature,
  no change log in the file.
- Document genuinely complex algorithms and business rules; skip everything else.
- TODO/FIXME carries context and what needs to happen - never a bare `// TODO`.
- Remove commented-out code before committing. Version control already has it.
- A comment that contradicts the code is worse than none. Update or delete it with the change.

## README Files

- Every project should have a `README.md` at the root
- Include: project description, setup instructions, usage, and contribution guidelines
- No emojis or icons unless the project explicitly requires them
- Keep it concise -- link to detailed docs rather than duplicating content

## API Documentation

- Document all public endpoints with method, path, request/response format
- Include example requests and responses
- Note required authentication and authorization
- Document error responses and status codes

## Doc Comments (Javadoc / KDoc / JSDoc / docstrings)

Required where the reader is outside the file, optional everywhere else.

- **Required**: public APIs, exported functions, interfaces, and anything published as a
  library. Use the language-native format (KDoc for Kotlin, Javadoc for Java, JSDoc for JS/TS,
  docstrings for Python).
- **Skip**: getters, setters, overrides that add nothing, and self-explanatory methods.
  A doc comment restating the method name is noise.
- Document parameters, return values and thrown exceptions **only where non-obvious** -
  a nullability rule, a unit, a range, an exception a caller must handle.
- Same length discipline as inline comments: a sentence or two. Long-form explanation goes in
  an ADR or the README, linked from the doc comment.

## Sources

- Markdown: CommonMark, https://spec.commonmark.org
- MADR: Oliver Kopp, Olaf Zimmermann et al., "Markdown Architectural Decision Records", https://adr.github.io/madr/
- Architecture Decision Records: Michael Nygard, "Documenting Architecture Decisions", 2011, https://cognitect.com/blog/2011/11/15/documenting-architecture-decisions
- Mermaid: Mermaid, https://mermaid.js.org
- Comments explain why, not what: John Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design*, 2018, ch.12-13; Steve McConnell, *Code Complete*, 2nd ed., 2004, ch.32
- No commented-out code: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code*, 2008, ch.4
- Javadoc: Oracle, "How to Write Doc Comments for the Javadoc Tool", https://www.oracle.com/technical-resources/articles/java/javadoc-tool.html
- KDoc: JetBrains, "Documenting Kotlin code", https://kotlinlang.org/docs/kotlin-doc.html
- JSDoc: JSDoc, https://jsdoc.app
- Docstrings: David Goodger and Guido van Rossum, PEP 257, 2001, https://peps.python.org/pep-0257/
